static_traits.name: Zhou Tairan
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, no immediate family mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends in the industry, but has not yet fully shared fears and self-doubt with them
static_traits.medical_history: Never received psychotherapy or had similar psychological problems; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly coherent logic; rather negative tone, skeptical; often uses absolutist and generalizing statements in conversation (e.g. 'forever' 'too old'), prone to comparison and self-denial, reasonably cooperative

basic_info.main_problem: Worries about age leave me with self-doubt and fear in my acting career.
basic_info.core_demands: Fear and self-doubt related to my acting career are affecting my mental health and performance, so I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: Filmed my first movie at 18, full of possibility and anticipation for the career early on; after 25, worries about age grew markedly, especially triggering at auditions; long influenced by entertainment-industry stereotypes about age and success plus social pressure, and constantly reinforced self-doubt and fear when seeing younger actors gain opportunities and success.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / not valuable enough
My age decides my career success or failure

special_situations.event: Seeing younger actors chosen or getting more attention at auditions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not young enough, I cannot be chosen, and have no room to grow
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to stay positive and focus on improving skills to prove myself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too old; I cannot be chosen

special_situations.event: Seeing younger actors' success and exposure in media or on social platforms
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they succeed, it means the industry only favors the young, and I basically have no chance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Comparing myself with younger actors, doubling practice hoping to close the gap
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The industry only favors young people; my time has already passed

special_situations.event: Noticing casting notices favoring younger actors
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If notices favor the young, I must not fit any role
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on age limits, ignoring positive evidence that one's experience is recognized
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I don't meet the requirements; I am too old

special_situations.event: Feeling compared and self-doubting when interacting with peers or chatting with colleagues on set
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as young or successful as them, they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sharing less of my real fears with friends, staying superficially positive for self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I'm no good / they look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and seen, to keep getting roles and career development opportunities
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and washed out due to age, ultimately failing and losing worth
defense_goal: Lowering expectations through caution and self-doubt to avoid facing the pain of being washed out; revealing less vulnerability for self-protection

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, an actor marginalized by the times
object_relations.object_representation: An industry and casting directors that prefer youth, are picky, and reject age

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites examining beliefs, finding evidence, or doing reality testing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that 'talking can't change industry realities', unconsciously reading the counselor's exploration as misunderstanding or denial of industry rules
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Restrained and rather calm tone, emphasizing 'the realities of the industry' and 'the rules are so', using general statements to avoid emotional experience and concrete personal evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether there are successful older actors or positive examples of my own
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Dismissing such examples as 'lucky or connected', believing they have nothing to do with me (devaluing positive evidence as coincidence)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using remarks like 'they're just lucky / connected' to downplay positive evidence; tone is flat, holding to existing conclusions, avoiding further exploration of personal possibilities.

manifestations: Believes that their 'time has passed', treats age as a decisive factor; under the industry's age stereotypes, finds it hard to see their own value and possibilities
outcomes: Changes in sleep and eating patterns
Audition performance and career opportunities affected

manifestations: Experiences a sense of restriction from industry structures and rules on personal choice and control
outcomes: Skeptical about change; sense of room for action shrinks

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats 'only the young have chances' and 'age determines success' as absolute truths
Using absolutist rules like 'must / should / that's just how the industry is' in expression

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Not fully sharing the extent of fear and self-doubt with friends
Stating in sessions 'not expecting much change'

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When invited to examine positive evidence, turns to talking about 'the reality of the industry', using macro-level discussion to avoid her own feelings and concrete examples

exception_events.target_problem: In audition situations, the client typically denies themselves due to age anxiety, confidence drops, affecting performance and opportunities.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When praised by a director on set for professionalism and experience, he felt more confident in the moment, anxiety eased, and saw that his worth could be recognized.
exception_events.reason: Different support: positive feedback from the director; different understanding: seeing experience as an advantage offering unique value.

exception_events.target_problem: When seeing younger actors succeed, the client typically falls into comparison and despair.
exception_events.unique_outcome: While focused on improving skills, he briefly experienced rising confidence, less comparison, and greater focus.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: shifting attention to skill practice and self-improvement; different situation: the task is controllable, feedback comes from one's own progress.

positive_force: Has many years of professional experience and professionalism; was once recognized by a director
Actively trying to stay positive and focus on improving skills
Has some industry friend resources usable for support
negative_force: Strong catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking, tending to negate positive evidence
Excessive comparison and self-denial, sensitive to age stereotypes
Skeptical attitude toward change, prone to rationalizing positive examples as 'having nothing to do with me'
Stress-induced disturbed sleep and eating rhythms, further weakening functional performance

target_behavior.behavior: Intense career-related anxiety and self-denying thoughts (e.g. 'I am too old' 'I'll never land a major role')
antecedent: Looking at casting notices favoring the young
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting the industry's age stereotypes as standards for self-evaluation, and catastrophizing and overgeneralizing about the future.
target_behavior.function: Escaping failure and shame to seek self-protection; lowering expectations through self-denial to reduce disappointment
target_behavior.consequence: Audition performance and opportunities affected, tense interpersonal relationships and peer interactions, declining career confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Changed sleep and eating patterns (fluctuating with career stress and anxiety)
antecedent: Rising comparison and self-doubt when seeing younger actors get opportunities
target_behavior.core_reason: Persistent anxiety and stress causing physiological rhythm disruption and elevated mind-body load.
target_behavior.function: Briefly easing tension or avoiding directly facing uncertainty and anxious feelings
target_behavior.consequence: Physical and mental state declining, further affecting professional performance and coping ability
